mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both teams simultaneously showing a recent-5 possession mean that is lower than their all-prior possession mean (both teams are in a low-possession recent regime). Within that joint condition, measure whether shots_on_target FOR is suppressed relative to all-prior for the possession-losing side, and shots_on_target AGAINST is elevated for the possession-conceding side.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' recent possession is below their long-run average, the combined shots_on_target FOR across both teams is suppressed relative to the combined all-prior baseline, suggesting a jointly compressed attacking output regime.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When a team's recent possession share drops materially below its long-run average (indicating a regime shift toward a more defensive or reactive posture), its shots-on-target production also falls relative to its long-run average, while the opponent's shots-on-target allowed rises. The joint pattern of possession-drop and shots-on-target divergence across both teams simultaneously is the signal of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition across two distinct observables (possession AND shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously. It is not reducible to one observable with one band — it requires the co-movement of possession and shots_on_target across both sides to be evaluated together.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, compute the ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR across all-prior and recent-5 windows. Condition on the case where Team A's ratio is declining (recent < all-prior) while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST is rising (recent > all-prior), and vice versa. Measure whether this asymmetric cross-team pattern is associated with a directional shift in goals FOR/AGAINST relative to baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's shot accuracy is declining while the opponent's defensive shots-on-target-allowed is rising, goals FOR for the accuracy-declining team are suppressed relative to what either observable alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: A team's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shot accuracy) interacts asymmetrically with the opponent's defensive solidity as measured by shots-on-target allowed. Specifically, when one team's shot accuracy (shots_on_target FOR / shots FOR) is trending downward in recent matches while the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST is trending upward, the joint signal differs from either observable read in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a ratio of two observables (shots_on_target / shots) for one team jointly conditioned against a different observable (shots_on_target AGAINST) for the opponent — a cross-team, cross-observable asymmetric relationship not reducible to any single-observable mirror or band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) both teams' fouls FOR all-prior being above the competition context fouls baseline, AND (b) the competition context cards_2h baseline. Measure whether the joint elevation of both teams' foul rates relative to competition context predicts cards_2h above the competition context cards_2h mean, beyond what a single-team foul rate comparison would capture.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams' foul rates exceed the competition baseline simultaneously, second-half cards rise above the competition context cards_2h mean, with the joint excess being greater than the sum of each team's individual foul-rate excess.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The second-half cards (cards_2h) rate for a match is jointly shaped by both teams' foul-production tendencies and the match's goal-scoring context. Specifically, when both teams have elevated foul rates relative to competition context AND the competition context shows a high second-half cards baseline, the combined cards_2h output rises non-linearly beyond what either team's foul rate or the competition baseline alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-team, two-observable relationship (fouls for both teams jointly conditioned against cards_2h) evaluated against a competition baseline. It is not a single observable against one band — it requires the interaction of both teams' foul tendencies together with the cards_2h outcome.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: For each team, condition on the joint state where possession FOR (recent-5) is above the competition context possession baseline, but shots FOR (recent-5) is below the team's own all-prior shots average. Within this joint condition, measure whether corner_kicks FOR is suppressed relative to the team's all-prior corner kick average.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team has above-average possession but below-average shots in recent matches, its corner kick production is suppressed relative to its long-run average, indicating that possession without penetration does not translate to corner volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Corner kick generation is jointly influenced by a team's possession share and its shots volume. When a team holds above-average possession but its shots volume is below its long-run average (suggesting possession without penetration), its corner kick production is suppressed relative to what possession alone would predict. This cross-observable interaction between possession, shots, and corners is the mechanism of interest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (possession, shots, corner_kicks) with a cross-observable conditioning logic — possession above baseline AND shots below own average — which cannot be reduced to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) Team A's goals FOR second half mean exceeds Team A's goals FOR first half mean (Team A is a second-half scorer), AND (b) Team B's goals AGAINST second half mean exceeds Team B's goals AGAINST first half mean (Team B concedes more in the second half). Measure whether the combined second-half goal environment exceeds the competition context full-match goal baseline proportionally more than the first-half environment.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's scoring is back-loaded and Team B's defensive vulnerability is also back-loaded, second-half goals in matches between such teams rise above what the full-match averages and competition context would predict, representing a non-linear amplification from the joint half-level alignment.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The within-match distribution of goals between first and second halves is asymmetric across the two teams in a way that depends on each team's half-specific goal rates jointly. When Team A scores a higher proportion of its goals in the second half (goals FOR second half > goals FOR first half) while Team B concedes a higher proportion in the second half (goals AGAINST second half > goals AGAINST first half), the second-half goal environment for Team A is amplified beyond what either team's full-match goal rate would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs. second half goals) evaluated jointly across both teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously — a two-team, two-half, asymmetric cross-observable structure not reducible to a single observable with one band.
